clue.text: One who composed part back to cover single arrangement

parts.note: J S Bach, the composer

indicators.note: back says the word for part is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a part in a play is a role
a hood is something that covers the head

explanation.surface: A composer reworks a section of a solo piece, turning it backwards and wrapping it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single arrangement' reads as a musical term after the composer, but it means the way an unmarried person lives.
explanation.definitionFit: Bachelorhood is the unmarried state, a single person's way of living.

clue.text: Take over home to which weary husband returns

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: returns tells us the word for weary comes back to front

parts.note: to weary is to tire

explanation.surface: A tired husband comes back to the house he is about to take charge of.
explanation.definitionFit: To inherit something is to take it over from a predecessor, typically on their death.

clue.text: Nasty women from Paris he messed around

indicators.note: messed around signals the letters being jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Unpleasant women from the French capital toy with a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Harpies are mythological winged monsters, and figuratively spiteful, grasping women.

clue.text: River claims factory director

indicators.note: claims means the river takes the factory into its middle

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a mill is a factory

explanation.surface: A river encroaches on the land of a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'factory' could suggest a works or plant, but the miller's building fits inside the river name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecil B DeMille was the Hollywood film director of epics such as The Ten Commandments.

clue.text: European move to oust grand foreign government

indicators.note: to oust means a letter is thrown out of the word for move

parts.note: to migrate is to move
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A European's relocation pushes out a major foreign regime.
explanation.definitionFit: An emirate is a state ruled by an emir, a form of Arab government.

clue.text: Blighty deports no-good bounder

indicators.note: deports means the letters for no-good are expelled from the country

parts.note: Blighty is old British army slang for England
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: Britain expels a worthless cad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deports' takes NG out of ENGLAND. 'bounder' looks like a cad, but it means a leaping animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is an African antelope, an animal that bounds along.

clue.text: As compilers perhaps noticing nothing strange

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters are made odd by being rearranged

parts.note: O, a zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: Seeing nothing odd, perhaps like the people who set puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword setters traditionally work under pseudonyms, keeping their identities disguised.

clue.text: Adventurer most weary needs to unwind

indicators.note: to unwind is to come undone, so these letters are loosened into a fresh order

explanation.surface: The most tired traveller needs to relax.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Sawyer is the adventurous boy hero of Mark Twain's novel.

clue.text: Refrain from insincere talk that involves hospital

indicators.note: that involves means the talk holds the hospital letter within it

parts.note: cant is hypocritical or insincere talk

explanation.surface: Stay away from hollow chatter about a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refrain' looks like a verb, as in hold back, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A chant is a repeated sung line, a refrain.

clue.text: Schedule backed by dog keeper

indicators.note: by means the dog stands beside the schedule, coming before it

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: backed says the schedule's word is run backwards

parts.note: a rota is a schedule of duties

explanation.surface: A timetable is supported by a dog handler.
explanation.definitionFit: A curator is a keeper of a museum or collection.

clue.text: He wrote less about truth (as may be deduced)

indicators.note: about means one word goes round the other

parts.note: the opposite of less is more, which the bracket invites us to work out
the opposite of truth is a lie, again worked out as the bracket says

explanation.surface: A writer produced less about honesty, as one might infer.
explanation.walkthrough: '(as may be deduced)' tells you to swap each clue word for its opposite rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Moliere was the great French comic playwright, author of Tartuffe.

clue.text: Soldiers in outfits who pursued Penelope

indicators.note: in places the soldiers inside the outfits

parts.note: suits are outfits
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Uniformed soldiers chased Odysseus's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Odyssey, Penelope was besieged by suitors wooing her while Odysseus was away.

clue.text: Die long time after Durbeyfield girl

indicators.note: after puts the long time behind the girl

parts.note: Tess Durbeyfield is Hardy's heroine in Tess of the d'Urbervilles
an era is a long period

explanation.surface: A girl dies long after her time, as in Hardy's tragic novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is a small cube, used in mosaics and in ancient times as a die.

clue.text: Hunt with Brookfield schoolmaster for food

parts.note: to fish is to hunt for something
and means with
Mr Chips teaches at Brookfield school in Goodbye, Mr Chips

explanation.surface: Searching with a fictional teacher for something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish and chips is the classic British takeaway meal.

clue.text: Crusher seizes half the territory

indicators.note: seizes means the snake grips the other piece inside itself

parts.note: a boa kills prey by crushing
hemi- is a prefix meaning half

explanation.surface: An oppressor grabs half the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crusher' is the constrictor snake, not a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohemia is a historical region, now part of the Czech Republic.

clue.text: Getting separated, copper on road took van

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to take the van, the vanguard, is to lead, so took van means led

explanation.surface: A police officer on the road drove a van while splitting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' is not a vehicle: it is the vanguard, the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk that has curdled has separated into curds and whey.

clue.text: Give out in attempt to succeed old member

indicators.note: to succeed means the attempt follows on after the old part

parts.note: ex- means former, old

indicators.note: in places the giving out inside the attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to emit is to give out

explanation.surface: Putting forth effort to replace a former member of a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' means a limb here, not someone belonging to a club.
explanation.definitionFit: An extremity is a limb, a hand or foot, and member is an old word for a limb.

clue.text: Paint runs in groove

indicators.note: in places the runs letter inside the groove

parts.note: an oche is the line or groove a darts player stands behind
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Paint drips into a channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy pigment used as a yellow or brown paint.

clue.text: Fish losing way at Humber's mouth

indicators.note: at means the straying part sits at the river letter, which leads
mouth means the start of the river name Humber

parts.note: erring means straying, losing one's way

explanation.surface: A fish goes astray at the mouth of the Humber estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: The Humber is an estuary in north-east England; its mouth is H, placed before ERRING.
explanation.definitionFit: The herring is a common North Atlantic food fish.

clue.text: Wherein folders hold paperwork?

parts.note: folders suggests office files, but these are people who fold paper into shapes, an art form

explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of folding paper into decorative figures.

clue.text: Tinker tolerates tripe

parts.note: to tinker is to fiddle with something
sticks means puts up with, tolerates

explanation.surface: A handyman puts up with offal.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddlesticks is an exclamation meaning nonsense, and tripe is slang for nonsense.

clue.text: Lose no time in suppressing the garrulous?

definitions.meaning: to hurry, from pressing a car's accelerator
read literally, treading down on someone's gassy talk, gas being idle chatter

explanation.definitionFit: Stepping on the gas means accelerating, and gas is also slang for empty talk.

clue.text: Catch Miro out using colour

indicators.note: out signals the letters breaking out of their order

explanation.surface: Spot the painter Miro at work with paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Chromatic means relating to or having colour.

clue.text: Swallow one drink

parts.note: the martin is a bird of the swallow family
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Gulp down a single drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like a verb but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka and vermouth.

clue.text: Sacred place — set it up in an old church

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the run that follows

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the word is turned to read upwards
set up in a down clue means the word is turned to read upwards

explanation.surface: Erect it inside an ancient church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns IT into TI, which goes into AN O CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch was a holy city of early Christianity, where believers were first called Christians.

clue.text: Conservative lives alone in retreat for major figures

indicators.note: in retreat means the words go backwards

parts.note: is means lives, exists
solo means alone

explanation.surface: A Tory lives in solitary seclusion away from the big names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' turns ISSOLO into OLOSSI, after C.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossi are huge statues, and figuratively people of great stature.

clue.text: Eternal promise of face-cream factors?

definitions.meaning: what skincare ingredients claim: age made less

explanation.definitionFit: Ageless means never growing old, which beauty creams claim to deliver.

clue.text: Right and wrong about Orff's first material for strings

indicators.note: first means just the opening letter of Orff

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: Correct and incorrect views on the composer Orff's early work for string players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts O inside SIN, after R.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosin is the resin rubbed on violin bows so the strings grip.
